maria: Quick sync — thinking about a 'meshlet' style canary where small local nodes can accept traffic and perform a local fallback before failing over to the global variant. Wanted to float the fallback contract so we don't get split-brain. PTAL.

dan: short version?

maria: TLDR: let local meshlets advertise a 'fallback-ready' boolean plus a lease attempt step. flow: local probe -> try lease -> if lease granted serve canary; if lease denied or probe fail -> return controlled fallback to global model. sketch below.

maria: ```
fallback_contract: 
  mode: meshlet-local-first
  signals: [p95_latency_ms, error_rate, kv_cache_staleness]
  lease_ttl: 5s
  cooldown: 30s
  reason_codes: [probe_timeout, lease_denied, capacity_exhausted]
```

olivia: I like the contract. main concern: two meshlets could both think they're allowed if leases overlap or clock skews. we need a cheap quorum or reuse existing pilot-lease service.

ryan: agree with olivia. reuse pilot-lease token. plus make lease_ttl conservative (5s ok if heartbeats are reliable). also we should gate on a metric delta threshold so noisy probes don't flipflop.

dan: +1 on metric delta. also add a max-fallback-rate per tenant so we don't cascade global traffic unexpectedly.

maria: good call. propose adding `max_fallback_per_minute` and `ramp_window` to the contract.

maria: updated sketch: ```
fallback_contract:
  mode: meshlet-local-first
  signals: [p95_latency_ms, error_rate]
  lease_source: pilot-lease:v2
  lease_ttl: 5s
  cooldown: 30s
  ramp_window: 2m
  max_fallback_per_minute: 10
  reason_codes: [probe_timeout, lease_denied, capacity_exhausted]
```

ryan: also expose tags on metrics: `fallback.origin=local|global`, `fallback.reason=lease_denied|probe_timeout`. makes alerting and SLO accounting cleaner.

olivia: observability note: include a sample of the input prompt hash to detect correlated regressions (PII-safe). store only prefix hash.

infra-bot: FYI: there's an ongoing pilot-lease rollout; current API is /v1/leases which supports 1s-60s TTLs.

maria: thanks — will target RFC PR that folds this into rollout-controller and the canary decision surface. I'll add unit tests for lease denial path and a short sim to show no double-serve under clock skew.

dan: can you also add a simple CLI check for local dev? `rctl canary-check --simulate-lease-deny` would help.

maria: yep, adding that to the PR. will ping owners when ready. :thumbsup:

ryan: nit: add a clear contract for partial responses (serve partial tokens vs immediate fallback). production teams will want an explicit behavior.

maria: good point — I'll add `partial_response_policy: [drain, fallback]` to options.

olivia: great. this feels implementable without a massive refactor. thanks all.
